metadata.description: Name of the resource group to create or reuse.
Azure region for every resource in the stack.
Prefix for resource names other than the independently named export storage account.

Optional environment token appended to resource names other than export storage, e.g. prod. Empty keeps the default naming (id-cloudlens, plan-cloudlens); setting it produces CL-id-prod, CL-plan-prod and so on. These names become deterministic, so deploy.ps1 checks the globally-unique ones for availability first.

Reviewed, stable export storage account name (3-24 lowercase letters/digits). Required: for a new deployment generate a random name once and save it in the parameters; for redeployment use the actual existing account, never a newly generated name. deploy.ps1 generates/persists or adopts this value.
Object ID of the Entra principal that becomes the PostgreSQL administrator. Usually the person or pipeline running this deployment.
Sign-in name of that administrator, e.g. someone@contoso.com.
Type of that administrator principal.
True for a customer deployment: PostgreSQL is injected into the virtual network and has no public endpoint. False for development: PostgreSQL keeps a public endpoint restricted by firewall rules.
IPv4 CIDR for the new VNet when networkIsolation is true. Choose a range that does not overlap networks it will connect to. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.

IPv4 CIDR for App Service integration, contained within the VNet and disjoint from the other subnets. Minimum subnet size /28; /26 or larger is recommended. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
IPv4 CIDR for PostgreSQL, contained within the VNet and disjoint from the other subnets. Minimum subnet size /28. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
IPv4 CIDR for private endpoints, contained within the VNet and disjoint from the other subnets, with sufficient usable addresses. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
Client IP allowed through the PostgreSQL firewall when networkIsolation is false. Ignored otherwise.
App Service plan SKU. B2 is the reference floor for the measured multi-million-row workload.
PostgreSQL compute SKU. The memory-optimised E2ds_v5 is the measured reference for large estates.
PostgreSQL major version. Central India offers 11-18.
Storage type. Premium_LRS ties IOPS to capacity; PremiumV2_LRS provisions IOPS and throughput independently of size.
Provisioned IOPS, PremiumV2_LRS only.
Provisioned throughput MB/sec, PremiumV2_LRS only.
Create a new `costs` table partitioned by month. Must be correct before the application first starts; it cannot convert an existing table.
Session work_mem for application connections. Empty keeps the server default.
Reader statement_timeout. The 25s default stays below the dashboard 30s client deadline; tune upward only after measuring legitimate query durations.
Ingest cost data on first boot when the warehouse is empty.
Calendar months to ingest automatically before an administrator chooses earlier history. Current month counts as one.
Run the daily refresh.
Warm recently used, private dashboard snapshots after a data generation changes. Bounded to three recent views per active browser.
Allow username/password sign-in alongside Entra.
Local accounts as name:hash:role, PBKDF2 hashed.
Schema the warehouse owns. Empty uses `public`.
PostgreSQL storage in GB. 128 GB is the measured reference capacity for large estates.
Region for the AI Foundry account. Rarely the same as `location`: the regions with App Service quota and the regions offering a model on a pay-as-you-go SKU are different sets.
Model deployed for the chat agent.
Model deployment SKU. GlobalStandard is pay-as-you-go; a region offering only GlobalProvisionedManaged needs a different aiLocation.
Tokens-per-minute quota, in thousands.

Create the Entra app registration people sign in through. Needs directory rights (Application Developer or higher); leave false where the identity team owns app registrations and pass an existing client ID to deploy.ps1 instead.
Display name for that app registration.
Stable unique name for it. Changing this creates a second registration rather than renaming the first.

True calls Azure as the signed-in person, so each sees exactly their own subscriptions. Needs one-time tenant admin consent for ARM `user_impersonation`; without it nobody can sign in. False is app-identity mode: the app resolves who holds a cost-capable role, bounded by the subscriptions its own identity reads.

The app creates its own FOCUS exports (one per visible subscription) and imports the last 3 months on first start; earlier months, up to 13, are optional from Setup. Needs Cost Management Contributor for the app identity on the monitored scope.
Tags applied to every resource.
Azure region for every resource.
Prefix for resource names.

Optional environment token appended to resource names other than storage. Empty keeps the default CAF naming (id-cloudlens); setting it brackets the type abbreviation instead (CL-id-prod). PostgreSQL is folded to lower case.
Stable, reviewed export storage name. Generate once for a new deployment; preserve the actual account name on redeployment.
Object ID of the Entra principal that becomes the PostgreSQL administrator.
Sign-in name of that administrator.
Type of that administrator principal.
Whether to deploy the network-isolated shape.
IPv4 CIDR for the new VNet when isolated. Must not overlap networks it will connect to. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
IPv4 CIDR for App Service integration, inside the VNet and disjoint from other subnets. Minimum size /28; /26 or larger recommended. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
IPv4 CIDR for PostgreSQL, inside the VNet and disjoint from other subnets. Minimum size /28. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
IPv4 CIDR for private endpoints, inside the VNet and disjoint from other subnets, with sufficient usable addresses. Preserve the deployed range on existing deployments.
Developer client IP allowed through the PostgreSQL firewall when not isolated.
App Service plan SKU.
PostgreSQL compute SKU.
PostgreSQL major version. Kept as a parameter rather than pinned: the local baseline this deployment is measured against runs 18, and silently deploying an older engine hides the difference.
Storage type. Premium_LRS welds IOPS to capacity (32GB = 120 IOPS, the trap the first deployment fell into); PremiumV2_LRS buys IOPS independently of size.
Provisioned IOPS. PremiumV2_LRS only; ignored for Premium_LRS, where IOPS follow the disk tier.
Provisioned storage throughput in MB/sec. PremiumV2_LRS only.
Create a new `costs` table partitioned by month. Read once at import; it cannot convert a table that already exists, so it must be correct before the application first starts.
Session work_mem for application connections. Empty keeps the server default. Applies per sort node and per pooled connection, so size it against the server, not the query.
Reader statement_timeout. Keep below the dashboard client deadline so abandoned reads return their pool slot promptly.

Let the application ingest cost data on first boot when the warehouse is empty. False for a deployment whose data is loaded by other means, so a boot cannot mix its own subscription into a restored estate.
Initial automatic ingestion history in calendar months, including the current month.
Run the daily refresh. False pins the warehouse to exactly what was loaded.
Warm recently used, private dashboard snapshots after a data generation changes.
Allow username/password sign-in alongside Entra. Production runs with this enabled.
Local accounts as name:hash:role, PBKDF2 hashed. Never a plaintext password.
Schema the warehouse owns. Empty uses `public`.
PostgreSQL storage in GB.
Region for the AI Foundry account, which is rarely the same as the app: the regions with App Service quota and the regions offering a model on a pay-as-you-go SKU are different sets.
Model deployed for the chat agent.
Model deployment SKU. GlobalStandard is pay-as-you-go; a region that only offers GlobalProvisionedManaged needs a different aiLocation.
Tokens-per-minute quota, in thousands.
True calls Azure as the signed-in person; false is app-identity mode. See main.bicep.
The app creates its own FOCUS exports and backfills history on first start. See main.bicep.
Tags applied to every resource.

variables.postgresName: [if(variables('bracketed'), toLower(format('{0}-postgres-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), parameters('nameSuffix'))), format('{0}-pg-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), variables('suffix')))]
variables.webAppName: [if(variables('bracketed'), format('{0}-web-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), parameters('nameSuffix')), format('{0}-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), variables('suffix')))]
variables.foundryName: [if(variables('bracketed'), format('{0}-aif-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), parameters('nameSuffix')), format('aif-{0}-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), variables('suffix')))]

resources.name: [format('{0}/{1}', if(variables('bracketed'), format('{0}-pe-blob-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), parameters('nameSuffix')), format('pe-{0}-blob', parameters('namePrefix'))), 'default')]
dependsOn: [resourceId('Microsoft.Network/privateEndpoints', if(variables('bracketed'), format('{0}-pe-blob-{1}', parameters('namePrefix'), parameters('nameSuffix')), format('pe-{0}-blob', parameters('namePrefix'))))]

properties.storage: [if(equals(parameters('postgresStorageType'), 'PremiumV2_LRS'), createObject('storageSizeGB', parameters('postgresStorageGb'), 'type', 'PremiumV2_LRS', 'iops', parameters('postgresIops'), 'throughput', parameters('postgresThroughput')), createObject('storageSizeGB', parameters('postgresStorageGb'), 'autoGrow', 'Enabled'))]

properties.condition: ((!(ActionMatches{'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'})) OR (@Request[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:RoleDefinitionId] ForAnyOfAnyValues:GuidEquals {ba92f5b4-2d11-453d-a403-e96b0029c9fe} AND @Request[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:PrincipalType] ForAnyOfAnyValues:StringEqualsIgnoreCase {'ServicePrincipal'})) AND ((!(ActionMatches{'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/delete'})) OR (@Resource[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:RoleDefinitionId] ForAnyOfAnyValues:GuidEquals {ba92f5b4-2d11-453d-a403-e96b0029c9fe} AND @Resource[Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments:PrincipalType] ForAnyOfAnyValues:StringEqualsIgnoreCase {'ServicePrincipal'}))
